key_insight: NeST co-designs high-rate quantum error-correcting codes with nested silicon-spin shuttling tracks to enable simulated stabiliser cycles below 50 μs.
engineering_relevance: Rigid, globally controlled qubit-train motions could provide the long-range connectivity needed for low-overhead fault tolerance on a square lattice of fabricated tracks.
method: Map non-abelian group operations onto nested conveyor-belt loops.
Search compatible qLDPC codes and simulate circuits with shuttling dephasing.
Construct a code-surgery gadget using only rigid belt motions.
evidence_signal: The search finds 20%-rate codes up to [[1400,280,≤28]]; circuit simulations report thresholds above 10⁻³, while a [[150,30,10]] surgery gadget adds 29% more gate layers without extra qubits.
watch_item: The projected 10⁻¹⁴ logical error probability per qubit per round is an extrapolation requiring tenfold improvement over early shuttling demonstrations and other physical errors at 0.1%.
paper_title: NeST: ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes with sub-$50μ$s stabiliser cycles via spin shuttling
